title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. In the 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)' notes, Grothendieck builds an axiomatic, combinatorial framework of 'ateliers' (workshops): a poset or category of 'figures' with a relation of incidence or separation between figures, meant to axiomatise tame stratified spaces. On p.88 he sets himself three tasks: (1) make the axioms explicit for an 'atelier ensembliste'; (2) check that they are stable under passage to sub-ateliers; (3) study saturation. An atelier ensembliste is a set L together with a set M of figures (subsets of L) and a symmetric relation X ≭_M Y on M, subject to At ens 1–3.

This page continues task (1), axiom by axiom.

(i) Degenerate case. Take M = { {x} | x ∈ L }, the singletons. Then the data reduces to a symmetric relation x ≭ y on L, and At ens 1–3 hold trivially.

(ii) Axiom At 9 in that case is (apparently) trivially verified. In the general set-theoretic case, At 9 translates into a locality axiom, labelled (*) and called At ens 4: if X, Y ∈ M and x ≭_M y for all x ∈ |X|, y ∈ |Y|, then X ≭_M Y. That is, separation of figures is detected pointwise.

(iii) Grothendieck notes that, given At ens 2, this is equivalent to the reformulation 'At ens 2 (or At ens 4)': if X, Y ∈ M and |X| ∩ |Y| = ∅, then X ≭_M Y (hence X ∥ Y). The margin concludes: 'En fait, on a donc X∥Y ssi |X|∩|Y|=∅'. So the relation ∥ coincides with disjointness of supports.

(iv) Relative version At 9_Σ, where Σ is a class of admissible 'intersection' sets. It translates into At ens 2_Σ (or At ens 4_Σ): for X, Y ∈ M, let K be the set of common elements (strata?) of X and Y. Then X ≭_M Y holds iff (or at least only if) |X| ∩ |Y| = K, i.e. X ≭_ens Y, and K ∈ Σ. Separation 'modulo a common part K' thus means: the figures meet exactly along K, and K is admissible.

Next page. Σ = all admissible sets gives At 9'. At 10 follows automatically, and the stability axiom At 13 under filtered limits becomes automatic in the finite case.

Purpose. This is bookkeeping: making the abstract atelier axioms concrete in the simplest (set-theoretic) model, as a test bed for examples and counterexamples.
errors: Possible internal tension. The singleton case is said to allow an arbitrary symmetric relation x≭y with At ens 1–3 trivially satisfied. Yet the later use of At ens 2 to convert the pointwise condition into |X|∩|Y|=∅ requires that, on points, x≭y means x≠y (or at least is implied by it). Either At ens 2 constrains the point relation more than the singleton remark suggests, or the equivalence needs that extra hypothesis. The page does not resolve this.

In At ens 2_Σ the text reads 'il faut [et suffit?] que'. Whether the condition is meant as necessary only, or as necessary and sufficient, is unclear from the handwriting. The parenthetical identification with X ≭_ens Y suggests an equivalence is intended.

ideas.what: Set-theoretic model ('atelier ensembliste') of an abstract atelier: figures as subsets of a set L with a symmetric separation relation
ideas.modern_name: closest: abstract simplicial/cell complexes or face posets with a disjointness (independence) relation; combinatorial models of tame/stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct counterpart; the atelier notion itself appears to be unpublished Grothendieck
ideas.where_published: Tame topology programme is announced in Esquisse d'un programme (1984) §5, but 'ateliers' do not appear there as far as I know

ideas.what: Locality axiom: separation of figures is detected pointwise (X≭Y if all their points are pairwise separated), equivalently disjoint supports imply separation
ideas.modern_name: locality / support condition; disjointness relation determined by supports

ideas.what: Relative separation modulo a common admissible part K ∈ Σ (figures meet exactly along an admissible K)
ideas.modern_name: closest: transversality / clean intersection along a common face; 'intersection of two simplices is a common face' condition in simplicial complexes

missed.claim: The whole axiomatics of 'ateliers', of which this page translates At 9 / At 9_Σ to the set-theoretic case, is an unpublished framework for tame topology. It was never developed or published. This page itself is only routine axiom translation inside it.
missed.quote: Atelier ensembliste ... At ens 2_Σ : soit K l'ens des ... communs à X et Y. Pour que X ≭_M Y, il faut [et suffit] que |X|∩|Y| = K (i.e. X ≭_ens Y) et K ∈ Σ.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mild interest to anyone reconstructing Grothendieck's 1986 programme for tame topology (o-minimal/stratified combinatorics). The content of this specific page is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine translation of abstract axioms into a set-theoretic model. The only point of interest is that it documents the unpublished 'atelier' axiomatics of the Analysis situs notes; no new theorem or connection appears on the page.
transcription_corrections: Throughout, 'Atomes' should read 'At ens' (atelier ensembliste). The handwriting is 'At ens 1 – At ens 3', 'At ens 2', 'At ens 4', 'At ens 2_Σ' (or 4_Σ), 'At ens 9_Σ'.
'donc le domaine [?] est ... symétrique' is better read as 'donc la donnée revient [à] celle d'une relation symétrique x ≭ y dans L'.
'At ens 9_Σ se traduit par' rather than 'Atomes 9_Σ'.
The final condition probably reads 'il faut et suffit que |X|∩|Y| = K (i.e. X ≭_ens Y) et K ∈ Σ'.
The phrase rendered 'K l'ensemble des [?] … communs' probably reads 'l'ens des [strates/éléments] communs à X et Y'; it is uncertain.
Inserted line near At 9 seems to read '...trivialement vérifié. Dans [le cas] général, il se traduit par'.
